An opposition political coalition, The Big Tent, has urged presidential candidates of opposition parties to unite and present a consensus candidate ahead of the January 16, 2027 presidential election. In a statement issued on Thursday in Abuja, the spokesman for the coalition, Toni Akeni, called on the opposition leaders to begin discussions on forming an inclusive cabinet-in-waiting to take over governance after the election. While assessing the political campaigns of various parties across the country, Akeni expressed confidence that President Bola Tinubu and the ruling All Progressives Congress would lose the election, claiming that Nigerians were dissatisfied with the administration. “This is not guesswork. Since the history books of Nigeria were opened in 1914, since her independence in 1960 to the present, no sitting president and ruling party has made Nigerians suffer such mass hardship, misgovernance agony, ballot vengeance bitterness and red cards of eviction anger by Nigeria’s citizens as the Tinubu administration has managed to do,” he said. He claimed that public dissatisfaction with the APC was evident across the country, alleging that opposition parties were attracting larger crowds at their campaign rallies. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “From North to South and East to West, the streets have spoken loud and clear. One thing is uppermost and dear. Legitimate voters’ verdict on the APC is damning and conclusive. They can’t wait for January 16, 2027, to boot the present ruling party out of power,” Akeni said. He further alleged that APC campaign rallies were poorly attended, while those of the Nigeria Democratic Congress and other opposition parties attracted large crowds. “Dissent against Tinubu’s APC is deafening on land and air. In homes, vehicles to work, offices, citizens’ discourses in the media, markets and malls,” he added. On the economy, Akeni accused the Tinubu administration of worsening poverty and accumulating unsustainable foreign debts, alleging that the government’s economic advisers were disconnected from the hardships facing Nigerians. 2027: Atiku demands independent audit of INEC’s AI system Obi can’t match Buhari’s popularity – Shettima Diana London: Tinubu should grant interviews to Nigerian journalists – Osinbajo’s ex-aide He also criticised the administration’s handling of insecurity, accusing it of failing to protect communities affected by terrorist attacks and banditry. “For nearly three and a half years, Tinubu’s APC displayed incredible unconcern, dissociation and insensitivity to millions of Nigerians drenched in the calamities and agonies of daily killings, unrelenting bloodshed and literally hundreds of communities violently sacked by colonies of barefaced terrorists and bandits,” he said. Akeni also cited what he described as the growing number of internally displaced persons across the country, claiming that 3.7 million Nigerians were living in about 3,900 displacement camps. He called on opposition presidential hopefuls, including former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, Peter Obi, Donald Duke, Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, Peter Agada and Omoyele Sowore, to put aside personal ambitions and work towards selecting a consensus candidate. “Your Excellencies most valiant and noble: Abubakar Atiku, the blessed eldest opposition presidential candidate at age 79, Peter Obi, Donald Duke, Sheyi Makinde, Peter Agada, Omoyele Sowore and the others, the hour has come and indeed has long been overdue when you must hold hands – not as politicians but as statesmen, all pride and self-serving considerations gone – and walk together to that Green-White-Green Table to give Nigerians one consensus presidential candidate,” he said. According to him, a united opposition would provide an opportunity to present a candidate capable of leading a government focused on addressing the country’s challenges. He said the opposition leaders had an opportunity to make a lasting contribution to Nigeria’s political history by prioritising national interest over personal ambitions. “Legacy awaits you at that table. Nigerians have spoken. APC’s pestilence is broken. Their spell is over. Do the needful. History is waiting,” Akeni added.
